payload.headline: Tesla at 385.46 after an 11.46% jump with no news; margins shrinking, still avoid

summary.thesis: The 11.46% jump to 385.46 came with no reported news. Meanwhile quarterly sales are flat, margins are falling and free cash flow has dropped. The stock now trades near the top of its own valuation history.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: wait, because the price sits just below a resistance zone (a level where sellers have stepped in before) and the trend is still marked as down.
summary.act_at: Long-term, re-examine near 293.94 only if margins recover. Swing, act only on a close above 404.4 or a pullback that holds 363.89–368.73.

payload.happening: Tesla closed at 385.46, up 11.46% on the day. There is no news since the last note to explain the move. The price is now close to its 20-day average of 384.49 and above its 50-day (376.17) and 200-day (381.53) averages, but all three averages are flat and the overall trend is still marked as down. The next earnings report is due on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Today's jump changes the price, not the business. The latest filed quarter (ended 2026-09-30, filed 2026-10-22) shows that sales growth stopped. Sales were down 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) over the last 12 months fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. Two filing-based warnings point the same way. Inventory is up 15% while sales are up 0%, and unsold cars can force price cuts. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, down from 33¢ three years ago. At risk: margins and cash generation if inventory forces discounts. Not at risk: the balance sheet. Tesla has 37.5B of net cash (cash minus debt) and 45.4B of liquidity, so funding is not a problem. The fear in the wider tech market noted by the macro view affects sentiment only. It does not change demand or margins.

worth.text: The two valuation methods give very different answers. A discounted cash flow model (DCF: today's value of the cash the business is expected to produce) puts fair value at 20.01 to 44.3, with a base case of 24.66. That is because it starts from only 3.3B of free cash flow. Even if growth starts at 30%, the DCF value is only 44.63. Tesla's own price-to-sales history (what investors paid per dollar of sales over 5 years) gives 203.8 / 293.94 / 399.81. At 385.46 the stock is near the top of that history, in the 63rd percentile of the last 5 years, at 14.7 times sales and 424.1 times trailing earnings. The filings note that the price needs about 51% a year growth, while the business delivered 3% a year over 3 years. So the gap between the methods comes down to one choice: value Tesla on its thin current cash flow, or on what the market has historically paid for its sales. Note: the data's valuation summary still quotes a price of 345.82, which is the 2026-11-20 options-chain price from before today's jump.
worth.key_assumption: With flat sales, the market keeps valuing Tesla at the low-to-middle part of its own 5-year price-to-sales range, not near the 399.81 top and not on its 3.3B of free cash flow.

bull: The balance sheet is strong. Tesla has 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity, so it can fund heavy spending without borrowing stress.
Sales over the last 12 months still grew, to 103.6B from 95.6B (8.3%), and analysts' next-year EPS (earnings per share) growth is 25%.

Options traders hold the most open call contracts at the 400 strike (14,601 open interest). Calls are bets on a rise, so some traders are positioned for the price to reach the 393.63–404.4 resistance zone.
bear: Quarterly sales fell 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago, while inventory rose 15%.
Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and 12-month free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B.
At 424.1 times trailing earnings, the price needs about 51% a year growth, against 3% a year delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the own-history high of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.66, so the jump made the stock more expensive, not cheaper.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.89–368.73), a level where buyers have stepped in 4 times. A close below it would end this rebound.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine at this level only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Sales have stalled, margins and cash flow are shrinking, and the price is near the top of its own valuation history. The business is graded D, and the committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The price is in the 380.15–389.95 zone, just under resistance at 393.63–404.4 (touched 5 times), and the trend is still marked as down. No trade until a close above 404.4, or a pullback that holds 363.89–368.73.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report, the next test of margins, inventory and cash. The options-implied moves (14.2% by 2026-12-18, 22.1% by 2027-02-19) were priced on 2026-11-20 at 345.82, before today's jump, so they understate how far the price could move from here.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth back toward the 15.78% seen two quarters ago.
Twelve-month free cash flow rises back toward 6.8B from 3.3B. That would lift the DCF values, which currently top out at 44.3.

The price falls to the 293.94 own-history midpoint while margins hold at or above 3.35%. That would revisit the long-term avoid. For the swing view, a close above the 408.62–417.44 resistance zone (touched 7 times) would revisit the wait.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid and wait. There has been no news since the previous note, which confirms the 11.46% jump to 385.46 is a price move with no business reason behind it.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
